title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket

evidence_packet.title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket
evidence_packet.lead: Lewis Rimmer was in an induced coma after being hit by a car and suffering life-changing injuries
evidence_packet.summary: Lewis Rimmer was in an induced coma after being hit by a car and suffering life-changing injuries
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket - BBC News Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Sarah and Lewis Rimmer, pictured with their daughters, have vowed to stay positive By Lauren Hirst North West Published 30 minutes ago Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night. Her husband Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket. The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through. Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot. "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on. "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime Daddy." Image source, Sarah Rimmer Image caption, Lewis Rimmer had been with his wife and two daughters shortly before he was hit In the following three weeks, medics reduced the sedation and each day Sarah would hope to hear the words "settled overnight", indicating he had progressed and was comfortable. "The next six weeks brought a whole new battle," she said. "Waking up, piecing together what had happened, learning to eat and drink again and slowly seeing the tubes and machines disappear. "The girls finally got to see their daddy and began to understand what had actually gone on." On the day of the incident on 27 October 2025, Lewis had taken the afternoon off work

Prescot: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 15:00 until 19:00 on Saturday 14 November. Kirkby: The Christmas lights switch-on will take place in the town centre from 16:30 to 19:30 on Friday 20 November. Greater Manchester Manchester: There will not be an official Christmas lights switch-on in Manchester, but the lights will be turned on across the city on Friday 6 November. Bury: The Rock Shopping Centre is marking its 15th year with a new tradition - its first Christmas parade and lights switch-on, on Saturday 7 November. Festivities start from 16:00 where visitors are asked to meet for the parade. title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: The NHS says rates have improved, but that too many women are still not getting checked
evidence_packet.summary: The NHS says rates have improved, but that too many women are still not getting checked
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP Tell us which stories we should cover in the North West

Dave Barron, 61, from Bramhall, in Greater Manchester, has been decorating his home for Halloween every year since 2011, and has been preparing this year's Back to the Future-themed display since May. Dave's efforts are all a tribute to his late wife, Catherine. Accepting donations from Halloween visitors, he has raised more than £55,000 for the Macmillan cancer charity, which cared for Catherine before she died in 2020. "Halloween is emotional for me," Dave said. "I miss Catherine tremendously. She'd think I'm an absolute lunatic, but she was always a big part of it and I think she'd be really proud." "I have been working on this year's Halloween display since May," he said. "And it does cost me a bit. "But It's a small price to pay if it helps people who are suffering with cancer." Image source, Dave Barron Image caption, Dave's Bramhall display features a raised stage with a full size drum set, electric guitar and real piano parts "Within the last decade it's just got it bigger and bigger and bigger," Dave said of his Halloween extravaganzas." Dave put on a Doctor Who-themed display last year, but said this year's had been the most challenging project yet. evidence_packet.title: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue - BBC News Image source, Getty Image caption, Leonard Benker Johnson was one of the best boxers of his generation By Christian Brooks and Georgie Docker , North West Published 31 October 2026 He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion. Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin. He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party. More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest. A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw. Johnson came out on top, beating fellow teenager Jerry Hogan with a third-round knockout. It marked the start of a career that would bring more than 90 victories. Image source, Getty Image caption, Johnson was the eldest of four siblings and was born on 22 October 1902 to a father from Sierra Leone and a mother from Ireland. Johnson's breakthrough came in 1925 when he defeated reigning British middleweight champion Roland Todd twice in seven months. title: Car driver who dragged head teacher to his death guilty of murder

evidence_packet.title: Car driver who dragged head teacher to his death guilty of murder
evidence_packet.lead: Simon Richardson is convicted of murdering head teacher Michael Mullins and will be sentenced on Monday
evidence_packet.summary: Simon Richardson is convicted of murdering head teacher Michael Mullins and will be sentenced on Monday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced

title: Ex-football chief admits offences linked to woman's drugging and rape by husband

evidence_packet.title: Ex-football chief admits offences linked to woman's drugging and rape by husband
evidence_packet.lead: Karl Lindsay resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged
evidence_packet.summary: Karl Lindsay resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former football club chief executive has pleaded guilty to offences relating to the drugging and raping of a woman by her husband and others Karl Lindsay, 56, who resigned from non-league Taunton Town Football Club in Somerset before he was charged, has admitted the offences, which happened between 2015 and 2025 Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Lindsay's offending related to the rape of the woman by her husband and others in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, and the administration of substances to stupefy her for the purpose of sexual acts The woman's husband, who is in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife, including rape The woman at the centre of the case was in court with one of her relatives and watched Lindsay intently as he entered his guilty pleas Three other men, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, Scotland, Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich, have already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings

evidence_packet.summary: Free travel for 11-16 is among the changes set to be introduced across the Bee Network
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester's Bee Network has announced a series of changes that will be rolled out across its services The measures include free bus travel for 11 to 16-year-olds, rail integration and longer-term plans for daily fare caps The changes are expected to begin in the coming months and build on the franchising of the region's bus network, which was brought back under local control by former mayor Andy Burnham Here is a look at the plans set to affect passengers over the coming months Train stations across the region will begin joining Greater Manchester's Bee Network from December, with work continuing in phases until 2030 Under plans announced by Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), the integration aims to improve rail services, reliability, infrastructure and the overall passenger experience

title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket

evidence_packet.title: Wife tells of husband's recovery from crash moments after buying lottery ticket
evidence_packet.lead: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Her husband Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in t
evidence_packet.summary: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Her husband Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning for three weeks, Sarah Rimmer would call the hospital where her husband was fighting for his life in the hope of being told the father-of-two had simply made it through the night Her husband Lewis was in an induced coma after being knocked down by a Range Rover in the car park of a Sainsbury's store in Bolton, Greater Manchester - just moments after he bought a lottery ticket The doting father was airlifted to the Royal Preston Hospital where his family were told he had just a 30% chance of pulling through Lewis spent weeks on life support and had more than 40 hours of surgery, including the amputation of his left foot "For three weeks, I couldn't hear his voice, tell him about the girls or ask him for advice," said Sarah, reflecting on how life had changed one year on "The girls couldn't understand why we couldn't Facetime Daddy."

evidence_packet.lead: Everton striker Thierno Barry has said he was relieved that his family were not at home when it was burgled while he played in a cup match His home in Greater Manchester was targeted while he was playing for Everton against Newcastle United in a Carabao Cup tie at the Hill Dickin
evidence_packet.summary: Everton striker Thierno Barry has said he was relieved that his family were not at home when it was burgled while he played in a cup match His home in Greater Manchester was targeted while he was playing for Everton against Newcastle United in a Carabao Cup tie at the Hill Dickin
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Everton striker Thierno Barry has said he was relieved that his family were not at home when it was burgled while he played in a cup match His home in Greater Manchester was targeted while he was playing for Everton against Newcastle United in a Carabao Cup tie at the Hill Dickinson stadium on Thursday The Frenchman, 24, posted on Instagram "things could have been much worse" had his partner and toddler not been in the stands A spokesman for Greater Manchester Police said an investigation was ongoing Barry posted that he would not put his family "at risk" in the future by posting about his life on social media He said: "Maybe I've been too open about my family's life and mine, potentially putting them at risk, all just to show my lifestyle and inspire others through my journey and success, hoping to motivate them to do the same

title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before peop
evidence_packet.summary: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before peop
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over a quarter of eligible women in the North West are missing breast cancer screening appointments The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP Tell us which stories we should cover in the North West

evidence_packet.evidence_text: As people up and down the country look forward to celebrating Halloween this evening, one Greater Manchester man takes the festivities further than most Dave Barron, 61, from Bramhall, in Greater Manchester, has been decorating his home for Halloween every year since 2011, and has been preparing this year's Back to the Future-themed display since May Dave's efforts are all a tribute to his late wife, Catherine. Accepting donations from Halloween visitors, he has raised more than £55,000 for the Macmillan cancer charity, which cared for Catherine before she died in 2020 "Halloween is emotional for me," Dave said. "I miss Catherine tremendously. She'd think I'm an absolute lunatic, but she was always a big part of it and I think she'd be really proud." "I have been working on this year's Halloween display since May," he said. "And it does cost me a bit "But It's a small price to pay if it helps people who are suffering with cancer."

evidence_packet.summary: He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin He later channelled the fighting spirit he
evidence_packet.evidence_text: He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A self-confessed "prepper" who stockpiles food and supplies in case of disaster, says people who mocked him just two years ago are now appreciating what he does, after government advice to stock around three days worth of food and water Dad-of-two Mike Chappell, from Burnley, Lancashire, has food, water and non-mains energy sources to last him and his family for 90 days in case of a disaster He said the government's advice was "a good starting point" but he would recommend no less than 30 days' supply The government issued advice on 22 October in a bid to encourage people in the UK to stock up in case of a national emergency Chappell said while he had previously been labelled "a nutter" by some, "now it's completely different" after "headline after headline about [issues such as] oil, food, drought" He said it was now "much more approachable" to talk to people about the subject of prepping

Anne Morris - from Knowsley, Merseyside - had endured a two-year battle with lung cancer before finally receiving the news her family had been praying for She was declared cancer-free and jetted off to Icmeler, Turkey, the very next day to celebrate with relatives But what should have been a joyous holiday ended into tragedy when Anne went into cardiac arrest three days after arriving. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The famous Manchester flats trapped in five years of scaffolding hell Once home to Oasis star Noel Gallagher, India House holds a special place in Manchester's history. But residents have been battling to find answers after six Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:34, 01 Nov 2026 Updated 06:47, 01 Nov 2026 A wall of metal scaffolding covers India House on Whitworth Street The massive structure is wrapped around the building like a tight hug, with ‘Danger’ and ‘Keep out’ signs at the back From the main road some say it looks like a construction site or a 'prison' - but India House has been part of Manchester’s story for more than a hundred years, and holds a special place in the city’s musical history with its links to Oasis star Noel Gallagher who lived there in The apartment block is where Noel wrote songs for Oasis albums Definitely Maybe and What’s the Story, Morning Glory First built between 1905 and 1912, it was a packing warehouse before being converted into flats from 1988. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The full story of the murder of Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins Simon Richardson forced the beloved educator's family to endure a painful Crown Court trial, too cowardly to admit his guilt. Following two weeks of evidence, jurors Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:32, 01 Nov 2026 Only two people know exactly what happened in the Volvo that hit Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins as he was dragged more than a mile down the road to his death One wept as she gave evidence from a Crown Court witness box, shielded by a screen. The other faces a life sentence for murder Beloved educator and dad-of-two Mr Mullins was killed in horrific circumstances, the details of which shocked a community and left trial jurors in tears Hit by Simon Richardson as he cycled home from work - before being dragged 1.3 miles under the car - Mr Mullins' life ended on a grass verge by the side of the road Horrified witnesses followed a trail of blood before finding him fatally injured. Now Mr Mullins' family - as well as colleagues, parents and children from the Trafford school - finally have justice

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Protesters and counter-demonstrators face off outside No 10 North in Manchester city centre The groups were kept apart by metal fences manned by dozens of police officers Add to preferred sources Comments News John Scheerhout Cr A group of more than a hundred people, many of them carrying Union Jack flags, gathered shortly after 12 noon outside Prime Minister Andy Burnham's northern HQ in Albert Square They were joined later by a larger group of counter demonstrators organised by Stand Up to Racism waving flags of Palestine. The two groups were kept apart by metal fences manned by dozens of police officers Both events passed off without serious incident although the Manchester Evening News witnessed one man being escorted away by police. GMP later said two people were arrested and later released without charge Police bosses said they had provided 'significant' resources thought to be in excess of the operations mounted for big football matches like the Manchester derby. But in the end far fewer protesters attended - police estimated 400 - than expected Greater Manchester Police bosses had authorised increase stop and search powers giving cops the power to order people to leave or face arrest. GMP said the 'vast majority of both sides caused no issues to our officers'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Merseyside Gran who got all-clear from cancer dies on holiday days later Anne Morris' family faces a huge bill Add to preferred sources News Emily Carubia Late reporter 08:43, 31 Oct 2026 View 3 Images Anne Morris, 63, suffered a fatal heart three day A grandmother who got the all-clear from cancer tragically died on holiday days later. Anne Morris - from Knowsley, Merseyside - had endured a two-year battle with lung cancer before finally receiving the news her family had been praying for She was declared cancer-free and jetted off to Icmeler, Turkey, the very next day to celebrate with relatives But what should have been a joyous holiday ended into tragedy when Anne went into cardiac arrest three days after arriving. Despite frantic attempts by her husband, Alan, and paramedics to save her, she suffered a second cardiac arrest while on life support and sadly passed away The family now faces a huge bill. Anne's travel insurance was rendered invalid, they said, after she had failed to declare previous medical conditions, including COPD and cataracts, on the policy Her loved ones are now desperately attempting to raise funds to cover a hospital bill of £33,500 and the costs of repatriating her body, reports the Liverpool Echo

Add to preferred sources Comm More than 1,200 homes could be built across Stockport’s green spaces if given the go ahead next week. Stockport council’s planning and highways committee is due to consider four planning applications that could see hundreds of homes built across the borough despite opposition and Two applications are in Woodford near Bramhall , while one is in Offerton. Another is near Hazel Grove . The applications would total 1,292 homes if approved In Woodford, one application put forward by Barratt Homes and David Wilson Homes wants to develop land on Upper Swineseye Farm and build potentially 455 homes, of which 50 per cent would be affordable. The plans were recommended for rejection by councillors for the area JAG Woodford Ltd and Russell LDP’s plans for land south of Chester Road were recommended for approval by officers but were also rejected by elected members. If given the go ahead, this could see 423 houses built alongside up to 72 apartments for those aged over 55, and a 72-bed c A total of 81 new homes could also be built off Jacksons Lane in Hazel Grove. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life 'The food was terrible - but it wasn't the food that was the problem, it was me' Nasser relied on his hands at work - now he is having to rebuild his life one step at a time View 3 Images Nasser Hussain relied on his hands for work - but now Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:12, 31 Oct 2026 As a highly-skilled electronics engineer, Nasser Hussain was reliant on his hands. The 58-year-old, from Bolton , would spend his days repairing intricate components that were often no bigger than a Then a series of health 'episodes' turned his life upside down. Having once been busy, independent and hands-on, Nasser can now feel completely exhausted from just a few hours of work "I thought I’d get through it and just go back to normal," he said. "But things are very different now. This is my new reality.” Nasser initially suffered multiple transient ischaemic attacks, which are often referred to as 'mini strokes'. He said: "I had a number of episodes before it really hit. At first, I just felt tired. I didn’t realise anything serious had happened." During one episode, Nasser's sense of taste changed. “I went to a takeaway I know well and thought the food was terrible,” he said. “But it wasn’t the food that was the problem, it was me.”

evidence_packet.summary: The Christie Hospital 'I lost all feeling from waist down': Man's devastating diagnosis after being sent home from A&E Paul King was diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer after months of unexplained back pain View 4 Images Paul King, 56, from Old Add to preferred sources Comm
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital 'I lost all feeling from waist down': Man's devastating diagnosis after being sent home from A&E Paul King was diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer after months of unexplained back pain View 4 Images Paul King, 56, from Old Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 06:34, 01 Nov 2026 A Trafford man who was sent home from A&E with suspected sciatica before losing all feeling from the waist down just 12 hours later has spoken about how an earlier diagnosis co Paul King, from Old Trafford , had been experiencing "severe back pain" for months before a scan finally revealed he had cancer on his spine and lungs Devastatingly, he was given less than a year to live. The cancer had spread from his prostate to other parts of his body and pressing on his spinal cord, causing him to lose all feeling below his waist But more than three years on, the 56-year-old is living with stage four cancer that is being managed with treatment. Paul believes earlier access to diagnostic scanning could have made a huge difference to his outcome He is sharing his experience as the Manchester Evening News joins forces with The Christie Charity to launch a £42.5m appeal to build a new cancer scanning centre at the Manchester cancer hospital

The two groups were kept apart by metal fences manned by dozens of police officers Both events passed off without serious incident although the Manchester Evening News witnessed one man being escorted away by police. Anne Morris - from Knowsley, Merseyside - had endured a two-year battle with lung cancer before finally receiving the news her family had been praying for She was declared cancer-free and jetted off to Icmeler, Turkey, the very next day to celebrate with relatives But what should have been a joyous holiday ended into tragedy when Anne went into cardiac arrest three days after arriving. Despite frantic attempts by her husband, Alan, and paramedics to save her, she suffered a second cardiac arrest while on life support and sadly passed away The family now faces a huge bill. Anne's travel insurance was rendered invalid, they said, after she had failed to declare previous medical conditions, including COPD and cataracts, on the policy Her loved ones are now desperately attempting to raise funds to cover a hospital bill of £33,500 and the costs of repatriating her body, reports the Liverpool Echo

The 58-year-old, from Bolton , would spend his days repairing intricate components that were often no bigger than a Then a series of health 'episodes' turned his life upside down. Having once been busy, independent and hands-on, Nasser can now feel completely exhausted from just a few hours of work "I thought I’d get through it and just go back to normal," he said. "But things are very different now. This is my new reality.” Nasser initially suffered multiple transient ischaemic attacks, which are often referred to as 'mini strokes'. Around eight hours earlier, she was discharged from Tameside Hospital after being told she had suspected tonsillitis Lila had been sent home with antibiotics and a throat spray for tonsillitis, despite showing ‘strong signs of meningitis’ during her many hours in the hospital’s A&E An inquest into the little girl's death concluded Lila died from pneumococcal meningitis streptococcal pneumonia. Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening

evidence_packet.title: Quarter of North West women still missing breast cancer screening
evidence_packet.lead: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 5
evidence_packet.summary: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 5
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The NHS said while uptake had improved slightly in the last year, 28.9% of women were still missing the potentially life-saving tests Breast screening can detect cancer before people may notice any signs and symptoms, and women are invited for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years after that until they are 71 Dr Paula Cowan, a GP and the regional medical director for primary care at NHS England in the North West, said "some people may be reluctant to come forward for a number of different reasons" but that "breast screening... detect cancer at an early stage" The NHS encourages women to continue to check their breasts regularly and to get any unusual changes to how they look and feel checked out by their GP

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
